answer:
Hypothesis (natural-language): Interviews are the most commonly used requirements elicitation technique in ML-enabled system projects. Among the 194 respondents who answered the Q9 elicitation-usage question, 97 (50.0%) indicated they use interviews — more than any other technique — versus Scenarios (75; 38.7%), Prototyping (75; 38.7%), Workshops/Meetings (74; 38.1%), Observation (64; 33.0%), and Other methods (11; 5.7%). Interviews also lead on the all-respondent denominator (97/276 = 35.1%). A 10,000-resample bootstrap gives interviews 50.0% with 95% CI [42.8, 57.2], and pairwise bootstrap contrasts show interviews are used significantly more often than every other technique (all difference CIs exclude 0). The stated anchor of 69.399% (CI [69.062, 69.735]) is not reproducible from this dataset — its ±0.337pp half-width implies an effective n ≈ 72,049, far beyond the 276 respondents — and no Q9 technique approaches 69.4% under either denominator; it is therefore treated as an external, non-reproducible reference and does not change the data-grounded conclusion that Interviews is the most commonly used elicitation technique.

Verification evidence (requested refinement 1 — "quoted" semantics proven, not assumed):
• All six Q9 columns are pure strings with exactly 3 distinct literals: `-77`, `not quoted`, `quoted`; 0 NaNs. `Others_Free` carries `-66` (82), `-99` (183), 1 NaN, and 11 free-text entries.
• The 82-row NA set: rows with `-77` in Q9_Interviews = 82, rows with `-77` in ALL six Q9 columns = 82, difference = 0 (identical pattern). Cross-tab Status × all-`-77`: Completed=164/0, Completed-after-break=24/0, Suspended=6 (answered)/82 (`-77`). Zero Completed or Completed-after-break rows contain `-77`/`-66` in the Q9 block, and those 82 rows all carry `-66` in `Others_Free` → NA set is exactly the 82 Suspended respondents who never reached Q9.
• Valid Q9 responders = 194; across these, every one of the six Q9 columns has 0 NaN, 0 `-77`, 0 `-66` → no valid row is missing any Q9 answer.

Result table (both denominators, bootstrap percentile 95% CI, seed 2026):
| technique | quoted (n=194) | % (valid) | CI valid | quoted (n=276) | % (all) | CI all |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Interviews | 97 | 50.000 | [42.784, 57.216] | 97 | 35.145 | [29.348, 40.580] |
| Scenarios | 75 | 38.660 | [31.959, 45.361] | 75 | 27.174 | [22.101, 32.609] |
| Prototyping | 75 | 38.660 | [31.959, 45.361] | 75 | 27.174 | [21.739, 32.609] |
| Workshops_Meetings | 74 | 38.144 | [31.443, 44.845] | 74 | 26.812 | [21.739, 32.246] |
| Observation | 64 | 32.990 | [26.289, 39.691] | 64 | 23.188 | [18.478, 28.261] |
| Others | 11 | 5.670 | [2.577, 9.278] | 11 | 3.986 | [1.812, 6.522] |

Pairwise bootstrap (Interviews vs each other technique, valid denominator): vs Scenarios +11.34 [1.55, 21.13]; vs Prototyping +11.34 [1.55, 20.62]; vs Workshops/Meetings +11.86 [3.61, 20.10]; vs Observation +17.01 [6.70, 27.32]; vs Others +44.33 [36.08, 52.06] — all exclude 0, so Interviews' top ranking is statistically supported.

payload.hypothesis: Interviews are the most commonly used requirements elicitation technique in ML-enabled system projects: 97 of 194 valid Q9 respondents indicated using interviews (50.0%; 35.1% of all 276), significantly more than Scenarios/Prototyping (38.7% each), Workshops/Meetings (38.1%), Observation (33.0%), and Others (5.7%).
payload.workflow: Loaded 276x202 survey CSV; verified Q9 columns are binary string literals {'-77','not quoted','quoted'} with 0 NaNs; confirmed the 82-row -77/-66 NA set is exactly Status='Suspended (22)' and no valid row has missing Q9 values (194 valid responders); computed quoted counts and percentages over valid (194) and all (276) denominators; 10,000-resample percentile bootstrap 95% CIs for both denominators; pairwise bootstrap contrasts confirming Interviews significantly outranks each other technique; documented that the 69.399% [69.062,69.735] anchor is unreproducible (implied n~72k) and treated as external reference.
